# E0319: ambiguous method

Two traits give the type a method of that name, so the call names the trait it means, as `Report.describe(o)`.

- Rule: [`traits.ambiguous-methods`](../../reference/11-traits.md#traits.ambiguous-methods)
- Reported at: the method's name.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0319:19
trait Report {
  fn describe(self) -> str
}

trait Audit {
  fn describe(self) -> str
}

type Order = { id: i64 }

impl Report for Order {
  fn describe(self) -> str { "order {self.id}" }
}

impl Audit for Order {
  fn describe(self) -> str { "audited order {self.id}" }
}

fn summary(o: Order) -> str { o.describe() }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
trait Report {
  fn describe(self) -> str
}

trait Audit {
  fn describe(self) -> str
}

type Order = { id: i64 }

impl Report for Order {
  fn describe(self) -> str { "order {self.id}" }
}

impl Audit for Order {
  fn describe(self) -> str { "audited order {self.id}" }
}

fn summary(o: Order) -> str { Report.describe(o) }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0319_ambiguous_method.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0319_ambiguous_method.lt):

```text
── AMBIGUOUS METHOD ─────────────────── E0319_ambiguous_method.lt:19:33  [E0319]

`describe` is a method of `Report` and `Audit`:

  19 │ fn summary(o: Order) -> str { o.describe() }
     │                                 ^^^^^^^^

Two traits give the type a method of that name, so the call names the trait it
means, as `Report.describe(o)`.

Two ways to fix it:

  1. Call `Report`'s `describe`:

  19 │ fn summary(o: Order) -> str { Report.describe(o) }
     │                               ++++++++++++++++ ~

  2. Call `Audit`'s `describe`:

  19 │ fn summary(o: Order) -> str { Audit.describe(o) }
     │                               +++++++++++++++ ~
```
